text:
maria: quick heads-up — saw steady memory growth on canary after enabling page-clipping yesterday. RSS climbs ~15% over 30m on the batch-gen benchmark :eyes:

maria: stacktrace looks like allocator churn rather than a classic leak. no huge retained objects in pprof heap, but free lists are growing. posting the minimal repro command we use: 
```
./bench/bin/batch-gen --model t5-small --seq 512 --batch 8 --iters 3000 --profile=alloc
```

infra-bot: alert: canary-12 memory increase detected (avg RSS +13% vs baseline). link: https://infra.internal/runs/76421

aj: thanks — can you paste a short excerpt of `pmap`/`smaps` or a heap profile link? if free lists are growing maybe page-clipping combined with our slab reservation is leaving more unmapped pages.

maria: pasted a tiny snippet from smaps below (sanitized):
```
AnonHugePages:         0 kB
Rss:              123456 kB
Pss:               98765 kB
KernelPageSize:     4096 kB
VmFlags: rd ex mr mw me sd
```
not super helpful on its own. Ben, you ran the same bench last week — any recollection?

ben: I ran a related run, saw a bump after ~1200 iters. saved two heapshots and a pprof link: https://pprof.internal/links/run-76399/heap / flamegraph attached. main diff looked like: +30% anon mapped pages attributed to `arena_alloc` path.

ben: quick note — when page-clipping is enabled we call `madvise(..., MADV_DONTNEED)` in the slab shrinker; that can show up as less RSS but more fragmented VM ranges depending on allocation pattern. could be interaction with `mprotect` alignment rounding in our allocator.

lisa: I can rerun with extra tracing. Which env flags do you want? `MALLOC_CONF`? `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX`? or should I enable `--alloc-trace` on the bench?

maria: please run two quick variants:
1) baseline (page-clipping OFF): `PAGE_CLIP=0 ./bench/bin/batch-gen ...`
2) page-clipping ON + force smaller arena: `PAGE_CLIP=1 MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 ./bench/bin/batch-gen ...`
Also run with `--profile=heapshot` every 500 iters and upload the *.heapshot.gz. That should help show growth shape.

aj: I'll also prepare a tiny patch that flips the page-clipping threshold to 128KB (from 64KB) so we can test if granularity matters. won't be intrusive.

lisa: running variant 1 now, will kick variant 2 once done. ETA ~25m. posting command I used for reproducibility: 
```
PAGE_CLIP=0 ./bench/bin/batch-gen --model t5-small --seq 512 --batch 8 --iters 3000 --profile=heapshot --heapshot-interval=500 \
  > /tmp/batchgen-pageclip0.log 2>&1 &
```

ben: fyi when you upload heapshots include the `pprof -dot` diff or the `pprof --alloc_space` summary. that shows retained vs active allocations which helped me.

lisa: variant 1 finished. quick summary: RSS stable, peak ~122MB. uploaded heapshots: https://files.internal/snap-1983456789-pageclip0.heapshot.gz

lisa: starting variant 2 with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 PAGE_CLIP=1 now.

maria: thanks — if variant 2 replays the growth, try adding `MALLOC_CONF=dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000` to see if kernel reclaim timing changes shape of the spike.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary-12 is currently running bench jobs. no new deploys in the last 6h.

aj: opened a draft PR with the threshold tweak and a micro-benchmark: https://git.internal/r/runtimer/patches/321 (WIP). I'll include reproducer script.

lisa: variant 2 finished — RSS drifted up to ~142MB over 30m, full heapshots at https://files.internal/snap-1983456789-pageclip1.heapshot.gz and logs at /tmp/batchgen-pageclip1.log

ben: looking at the uploaded heapshots now. initial glance: retained anonymous memory increases in the `arena_large` buckets. not plain fragmentation — some allocations are never freed for long-lived caches. can you grep the logs for `cache_insert` patterns?

lisa: grep shows a short burst of `cache_insert` at warmup then periodic increases every ~400 iters. maybe our batching changed distribution.

maria: good work. action items:
- aj: please land the threshold tweak + add a CI micro-benchmark (assign to you)
- lisa: upload full pprof dot diffs and attach the `heapshot` timestamps to the infra run (assign to you)
- ben: follow up on whether this is fragmentation vs retained cache; if fragmentation, propose a mitigation (e.g., smaller arenas or forced madvise cadence)

aj: on it. I'll also add a 512-token synthetic that forces different tokenization boundaries to mimic batch-gen pattern.

lisa: noted, will attach diffs in the run page and ping again when it's all uploaded. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team — keeping this thread for async updates. I'll close when PR + heapshots are in.

aj: FYI I started a smaller quick-run locally with the new threshold, looks promising (RSS decreases ~8%). will post numbers later.

ben: cool — if local looks good, we can try canary with the patch and compare percentiles.

lisa: uploaded diffs and linked them in the infra run. last link: https://infra.internal/runs/76421#artifacts

maria: closing note — please set `assignee:eng-runtime` on the PR and tag `memory-bisect` in the issue.

maria: thanks again :heart:
